items.stem: Why should physics-related movement use FixedUpdate rather than Update in Unity?

options.text: FixedUpdate runs on the physics timestep, giving consistent, frame-rate-independent physics
options.rationale: Correct: physics should be driven on the fixed timestep.

items.explanation: Correct: physics should be driven on the fixed timestep.

items.stem: What is required for two Unity objects to generate a physics collision?

options.text: Appropriate colliders, with at least one having a Rigidbody
options.rationale: Correct: colliders define shape and a Rigidbody enables physics interaction.

options.text: Only a script with no components
A UI Canvas on each object
options.rationale: Canvas is for UI, not collisions.

items.stem: Which statements about Unity prefabs are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A prefab is a reusable template you can instantiate many times
options.rationale: Correct: prefabs promote reuse and consistency.

options.text: Editing the prefab asset updates its instances
options.rationale: Correct: changes to the source propagate to instances.

options.text: Prefabs cannot be instantiated at runtime
options.rationale: False; Instantiate spawns prefabs at runtime.

options.text: Each prefab can exist only once in a scene
options.rationale: False; you can place many instances.

items.explanation: Correct: prefabs promote reuse and consistency.; Correct: changes to the source propagate to instances.
